transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Yeah… I guess things have been harder at home lately. My father-in-law moved in with us, and I’m managing at work, but outside of that I’ve been more wound up, more short with people than I like. Coursework has been harder to keep up with too.

I’ve also stopped doing some of the things that usually help me clear my head, like fishing, woodworking, first-aid workshops… so I figured I should come in before it gets worse.
Have you been feeling sad or down most of the time lately?
Not most of the time, no. I get… frustrated, maybe worn down, but I wouldn’t say sad all day or anything like that.
Have you been feeling anxious lately?

Yeah… anxious, I guess, in the sense that I’ve been more wound up. Since my father-in-law moved in, I’m keeping it together at work, but at home and with my coursework I get short more easily. I’ve also been skipping the things that usually settle me down, like fishing and woodworking.
Are you avoiding certain situations or activities because you feel anxious or uncomfortable?

Yeah… somewhat. I’ve been skipping the stuff I usually do to clear my head—fishing, woodworking, those first-aid workshops. It’s not like I’m afraid of them exactly, I just feel wound up and I don’t end up going. Since my father-in-law moved in, that’s been happening more.
Has something specific and disturbing happened to you recently or in the past that's been on your mind?

Not disturbing like… a trauma or anything. It’s more that since my father-in-law moved in with us, things have been harder. I’m holding it together at work, but at home and with my coursework I’m more wound up and short than usual. And I’ve stopped doing the fishing, woodworking, and first-aid workshops that usually help me keep my head clear.
Are you skipping those activities because you're afraid of something happening or because you just don't feel like doing them?

More just… I don’t feel up to them. It’s not that I’m scared something’s going to happen. Since my father-in-law moved in, I’m just more wound up, and I end up skipping the things that usually clear my head.
Have you been having any recurring, intrusive thoughts lately?
Not really… I mean, I think about the situation a lot, but I wouldn’t call it intrusive. It’s more just there when things are quiet.
Are you avoiding those activities because of fear that something might happen if you do them?

No… not really fear. It’s more that since my father-in-law moved in, I’m just worn down and wound up, and I end up not going. Those things usually help me clear my head, but lately I just haven’t been doing them.
Have you been having any repetitive behaviors that you feel compelled to do?
No… I don’t think so. Nothing I feel like I have to repeat or check or anything like that.
How long have you been feeling this way since your father-in-law moved in?
About four months, I guess… pretty much since he moved into our house.
Have you noticed any significant problems in your relationships or daily life since you started feeling wound up and skipping your usual activities?

Yeah… a bit. I mean, I’m still getting to my EMT shifts and doing my job, but I’ve fallen behind on some paramedic coursework. And I haven’t been showing up as regularly for the community first-aid workshops I usually help with. That’s not really like me.
Would you say that your current state is causing significant distress or problems in your daily life?

Yeah… I’d say it’s causing some problems. I’m still getting through my EMT work, but I’ve slipped behind on my paramedic coursework, and I haven’t been as consistent with the community first-aid workshops I usually help with.
Has anything traumatic happened to you in the past?
Not really… I mean, nothing I’d call traumatic. I’ve seen rough things at work, but that’s kind of part of the job. Nothing specific comes to mind.
Are there any situations or places that you're avoiding because they make you feel anxious or uncomfortable?

Yeah… I guess I’ve been avoiding the usual stuff more than places exactly. Since my father-in-law moved in, I’ve been kind of wound up, and I just haven’t been going fishing, or doing woodworking, or showing up for the first-aid workshops like I normally would. Work I still do, but outside of that I’ve been pulling back.
Do you think your anxiety and avoidance of activities would stop if the situation with your father-in-law improved or resolved?

I’m not really sure yet. There hasn’t been a stopping point, since he’s still living with us and we’re still figuring out the caregiving routine. Maybe if that settled down, things would ease up… but I don’t know.
Do you think the stress of your father-in-law moving in is the main reason you're feeling anxious and avoiding your usual activities?

Yeah… I think so. It really seemed to start after he moved in. I’m still managing at work, but at home and with my coursework I’ve been more wound up and short than usual. And I’ve been skipping the things that normally help me clear my head, like fishing, woodworking, the first-aid workshops. So… yeah, that seems like the main thing.
Do you think your anxiety would go away if the stress with your father-in-law was completely resolved?
I don’t really know. There hasn’t been a clear stopping point yet… he’s still living with us, and we’re still kind of figuring out the caregiving setup. So it’s hard to say if it would just go away.
Do you think your anxiety and avoidance of activities are a direct response to the stress of your father-in-law moving in?

Yeah… I think it is. Since he moved in, I’ve been keeping it together at work, but at home and with my coursework I’m more wound up, more short with people. And I’ve stopped doing the things that usually help me settle down, like fishing and woodworking. So… yeah, it feels connected.
Have you been experiencing these feelings of being wound up and avoiding activities for more than 6 months?
No… not more than six months. It’s been about four months, I guess—since my father-in-law moved into the house.
Do you think your feelings of being wound up and avoiding activities will continue if they last for six months or more?

I’m not really sure. There hasn’t been a real stopping point yet… my father-in-law’s still living with us, and we’re still figuring out the caregiving. So I guess I don’t know what it looks like after that.
